title: Concept model A: force and mass
subject: science
phenomenonOrContext: The same fan pushes two carts of different mass; the lighter cart changes speed more each second.
lessonGoal: Use controlled data and a force model to explain how net force and mass affect acceleration.
successCriteria: I reason from net force, not from one force by itself.
I use evidence to compare acceleration when one variable changes.
I apply the relationship to a new case.

vocabulary.definition: the vector sum of all forces acting on an object
the rate at which velocity changes
a measure of matter and inertia that does not change with location
the gravitational force acting on an object

sections.title: NOTICE — Same fan setting, different carts
sections.body: A simplified cart model uses a level track with friction treated as negligible. The fan provides the stated net horizontal force.

data.provenance: Manuel Academy instructional model using a = Fnet / m. Values are model outputs, not experimental measurements.

items.prompt: Which pair best isolates the effect of mass on acceleration?

sections.title: FEEDBACK — Compare like with like
sections.body: To isolate mass, choose trials with the same net force and different masses. If both net force and mass change, the data cannot show which change produced the acceleration difference.

sections.title: LEARN — Two linked patterns
sections.body: For a fixed mass, greater net force produces greater acceleration. For a fixed net force, greater mass produces less acceleration. Acceleration points in the direction of the net force. Net force matters because forces in opposite directions can partially or completely cancel. Mass stays the same when location changes; weight can change when gravitational field strength changes.

reference.rightArrow: 6 N fan force to the right
reference.leftArrow: 2 N friction force to the left
reference.vertical: Upward support force and downward weight balance; they do not create horizontal acceleration.
reference.readingRule: Arrow direction and written magnitudes carry the meaning; no color is required.

items.prompt: Model task: connect forces, mass, and acceleration.

steps: Combine horizontal forces: 6 N right minus 2 N left gives 4 N net right.
Use the 2 kg mass from Trial B.
Calculate acceleration: 4 N / 2 kg = 2 m/s² right.
Check the direction: acceleration is right because net force is right.
State the model limit: treating friction as a steady 2 N and the cart as one object simplifies the real system.

sections.title: YOUR TURN — Calculate from net force
sections.body: A 3 kg cart has 10 N right and 4 N left acting horizontally. Vertical forces balance.

items.prompt: What is the cart's acceleration magnitude in m/s²?

sections.title: FEEDBACK — Do not use one force alone
sections.body: First combine the opposing horizontal forces to find net force. Then divide that net force by mass. If you divided 10 N by 3 kg, your calculation used the applied force rather than the net force.

sections.title: APPLY — Loading a delivery robot
sections.body: A delivery robot experiences the same 12 N forward net force before and after a package is added. Its total mass changes from 6 kg to 9 kg.

items.prompt: Compare the two accelerations, cite calculated values, and explain why the package changes acceleration but does not change the direction.

sections.title: FEEDBACK — Connect the ratio to the mechanism
sections.body: A strong response calculates each acceleration from the same net force and shows that the larger mass accelerates less. The direction remains forward because the net force direction did not change.

sections.title: WHAT YOU LEARNED
sections.body: Acceleration increases with net force and decreases with mass. It points in the net-force direction.

sections.title: EVIDENCE YOU USED
sections.body: You used controlled cart trials, a labeled force model, units, and calculated acceleration ratios.

sections.title: HOW YOU DID
sections.body: Your saved numeric and written responses show whether you used net force and controlled variables. They remain pending assessment; the worked example alone is not mastery.

sections.title: WHAT TO PRACTICE
sections.body: Practice combining force vectors before using the force-mass-acceleration relationship.

items.prompt: A cart's mass doubles while its net force stays constant. Which change is predicted?

choices.label: Its acceleration is cut in half.
Its mass becomes weight and acceleration is unchanged.
